title: Prescribed-endpoint Hamiltonian paths in Cartesian products of directed cycles
scope: Refutes the prescribed-endpoint Hamiltonian-path characterization for Cartesian products of directed cycles: even for k=3, lengths(2,2,3), and distinct vertices u=(0,0,0),v=(0,0,1), directed distance1 satisfies distance congruent to -1 modulo gcd(2,2,3)=1, but no directed Hamiltonian path exists from u to v. Vertices are the actual dependent Cartesian product and arcs advance exactly one coordinate modulo its length; directed digons include both arcs. The result refutes both the displayed universal statement and its distinct-endpoint interpretation, with all factors of size>=2.
